judge_assessment.explanation: I recomputed all eight results at full precision and every one matches the printed answer at the requested rounding: 40*tan32 = 24.9948 giving 24.99 ft; 85/tan12 = 399.8936 giving 399.9 m; atan(3/20) = 8.5308 giving 8.5 degrees; 24/45 = 8/15 exactly; 150*sin28 = 70.4207 giving 70.42 ft (routed through the triangle solver from C = 90, A = 28, c = 150); 3200/tan15 = 11942.56 giving 11943 ft; 1.6 + 12*tan38 = 10.9754 giving 10.98 m with the eye height correctly added outside the ratio; and 50/tan20 - 50/tan35 = 137.3739 - 71.4074 = 65.9665 giving 65.97 m. All eight study-guide boxes check too (62.93, 16.3, 276.99, 78.32, 27.98, 15.5, 257.34, 29.28). The judge's two specific claims - that the eye-height adjustment and the two-boat difference were recomputed, and that the diagrams distinguish elevation from depression - are both supported: problem 7's 1.6 m is added after the triangle is solved, and the single value-free reference diagram in the directions labels both angles from the horizontal. I found nothing to add to or subtract from the judge's assessment.

strengths_to_preserve: Problems 1 and 5 are deliberately near-identical in wording, and the only thing that separates them is whether the given length is measured along the ground (40 ft, adjacent, tangent) or is a taut string (150 ft, hypotenuse, sine). The key names the pairing explicitly as a teaching note and adds the sanity check that a kite's height can never exceed its string. This is the single most useful design decision on the sheet.

All nine misconception traps are declared as expressions rather than typed numbers, so every line of the key's 'Common wrong answers' block (21.2, 18.07, 81.47, 1.875, 79.76, 9.38, 186.6, 208.78) is machine-derived from the wrong method and cannot drift from the misconception it describes.

The key's wrong answers come with a physical sanity check rather than a label: 18.07 m is refuted by 'a 12 degree sight line is very shallow, so the boat must be far out'; 81.47 degrees is 'the angle the ramp makes with the vertical - a ramp you could not walk up is the tell'; 208.78 m is 'the answer to a different picture, with the boats on opposite sides of the cliff'.

The reference elevation/depression diagram is printed once with the directions and is value-free, so no figure can be misread as carrying a problem's givens; every answer line prints its unit (ft, m, degrees), every unit is declared as answer_unit, and the binding is gate-checked in both directions.
Problem 4 asks for tan(theta) as a reduced fraction and the key defends why: 'the ratio is the exact answer. Turning it into 28.07 degrees throws away exactness and was not asked for.'
case_summary: A clean ACCEPT with no meaningful defect found. All eight worksheet answers and all eight study-guide answers were independently recomputed and agree exactly at the printed precision; the standards tags HSG-SRT.C.6 and HSG-SRT.C.8 are taken verbatim from references/standards-map.md and match the contract's HSG-SRT.C.6-C.8; every problem states its givens, its unit and its rounding; every unit is declared and bound on both the worksheet answer line and the key's boxed answer; and the whole gate chain is green with no manual items - correctly, because nothing on this sheet asks for an unverifiable written response. The problem 1-versus-5 tangent/sine pairing and the nine machine-derived traps are the two things most worth carrying to other cases.
